To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nuclear receptor, liver X receptor beta, interacts with and modulates the signaling of the endothelial-specific Tgf-beta receptor ALK-1.
the nuclear receptor LXBeta interacts with the TGF-beta receptor ALK1 and modulates ALK1 signaling in a novel manner.
the cytoplasm-localized LXRbeta is phosphorylated by ALK-2/ALK-1 and subsequently translocates to the nuclear compartment to modulate ALK-2- and ALK1-mediated transcriptional responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which endothelial cell-specific receptors signal in endothelia.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate angiogenesis, and in particular the role of the nuclear receptor LKRbeta in the control of endothelial cell function.
the identification and characterization of a novel mechanism by which the endothelial-specific TbetaR, ALK- 1, signals in endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ALK-1 is a TGF-beta type I receptor and LXR-beta is a nuclear receptor that modulates ALK-1 function.
LXR-beta is a modulator/ mediator of ALK- 1 signaling and that the ALK1-LXRbeta interaction may be a critical event in the regulation of angiogenesis.
ALK-1 is a receptor for a ligand that is not TGF-beta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALK-1 is a TGF-beta receptor that signals through the LXR nuclear receptor.
LXRbeta is a novel mediator of ALK- signaling.
ALK-1 is a TGF-beta receptor that signals in response to Tbeta1, Tbeta2, and Tbeta3.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear receptor LXBbeta can modulate signaling by TGF-beta receptors ALK-1 (and ALK-2).
ALK-1 signals in endothelial cells by interacting with LXRbeta and that the LXRbeta-ALK-1 interaction is essential for ALK-1 to signal in endothelial cell.
ALK-1 is a novel ligand for LXRbeta, and this ligand-receptor interaction is important in endothelial cells.
